correctness.rationale: For every order, uniqueness of cyclic h-factors forces any nontrivial closed factor border to have length below h; each starting index and border length gives at most one complete first return, proving the uniform upper bound. The lower bound is proved by the longest-closed-suffix injection. At order five, each Eulerian circuit corresponds to one of \(2^{16}\) vertex pairings whose 32-edge successor permutation is one cycle. Independently enumerated Euler walks yield exactly the same \(2048\) cycles. Across all circular factors, 2 independent border predicates and first-return enumeration agree on the histogram (93:360,94:888,95:600,96:200); exact rational moments follow algebraically.

value.rationale: The number of closed factors (complete first returns) is a natural, independently studied combinatorial invariant. The order-independent \(O(N\log N)\) constraint highlights the distinction between universal cycles and unrestricted quadratic-rich words; the first nontrivial multi-thousand-cycle census gives an exact, narrowly clustered distribution rather than a mere individual example or minor numerical increment. The exact finite classification is self-contained and motivates return-word studies at higher de Bruijn orders.
